question.text: The forward-bias voltage of a diode is changed from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>7</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">V</mi></math>, the current changes from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mA</mi></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>15</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mA</mi></math>. What is the value of the forward bias resistance?

solution.text:
The forward biased resistance of a diode is

R=∆V∆I=0.7-0.615-5×10-3

R=0.110×10-3=10 Ω
